title: A Superconducting Peierls Instability
authors: Pramodh Senarath Yapa, Joseph Maciejko, Frank Marsiglio, Annica M. Black-Schaffer
abstract: The Peierls instability is a foundational mechanism in condensed matter physics, showing how the electron--phonon interaction can transform a simple metal into an insulating state with a new lattice periodicity. In a one-dimensional (1D) metal the Peierls instability follows from the enhanced electronic response at wavevector $Q=2k_F$ (connecting the Fermi points) producing a Kohn anomaly: a softening of the phonon mode at the same wavevector. Condensation of this mode then generates the tell-tale Peierls periodic lattice distortion and charge-density wave (CDW) that gaps the electronic spectrum. Here we show an analogous instability at the edge of a two-dimensional (2D) superconductor, where a dispersing Andreev bound state (ABS) hosts Bogoliubov Fermi points at $\pm k_c$. The enhanced quasiparticle response at the connecting wavevector $Q=2k_c$ couples directly to pairing-fluctuations and produces a superconducting Kohn anomaly: a softening of a pairing mode at the same wavevector. Condensation of this mode then generates an edge pair-density wave (PDW) that gaps the ABS. We refer to this as a superconducting Peierls instability and identify the boundary quasiparticle structure that enables it. As a concrete realization, we consider a square-lattice extended Hubbard model whose mixed-symmetry $s+d+ip$ state hosts a dispersing ABS with zero-energy crossings at finite edge momenta. Using self-consistent Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) calculations we show that the order parameter develops an edge PDW, with the wavevector set by the superconducting Kohn anomaly, that gaps the ABS crossings. Our results identify a novel mechanism for spontaneous translation-symmetry breaking in a superconductor. As this superconducting Peierls mechanism does not require an extensive zero-energy flat band or topologically protected edge states, it may apply broadly to unconventional superconductors.
summary: This work establishes a superconducting Peierls instability, drawing an analogy between the metal-insulator transition and the formation of an edge Pair-Density Wave (PDW) in superconductors. By analyzing the instability of Andreev Bound States (ABS) at the boundary of a 2D superconductor, the authors demonstrate a novel mechanism for spontaneous symmetry breaking. This mechanism is computationally verified using the extended Hubbard model and suggests a broad applicability beyond specialized topological systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the superconducting analog of the Peierls instability, showing how an electronic instability at the edge of a superconductor can induce a gap-opening Pair-Density Wave (PDW).
main_result: The instability leads to the spontaneous formation of an edge PDW, which gaps the dispersing Andreev Bound States (ABS) at the boundary, representing a novel mechanism for translation-symmetry breaking in superconductors.
method: The analysis uses self-consistent Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) calculations and examines the instability of the edge state against pairing fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a square-lattice extended Hubbard model, focusing on a mixed-symmetry s+d+ip superconducting state on a ribbon geometry.
key_observables: Superconducting Kohn anomaly (softening of a pairing mode), edge PDW gap ($\Delta_{	ext{PDW}}$), and the gapping of the ABS spectrum.
important_parameters: The instability is driven by the zero-energy crossings of a *dispersing* ABS, which is key to its broad applicability.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory and focuses on the boundary realization, which is distinct from previous flat-band or topologically protected examples.
figures_summary: Figures schematically compare the conventional Peierls instability (CDW) with the superconducting analog (edge PDW). BdG calculations confirm the self-consistent development of the edge PDW structure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the analogy to the Peierls instability, then develops the superconducting counterpart by analyzing pairing fluctuations and the superconducting Kohn anomaly. Finally, it uses BdG calculations on the extended Hubbard model to confirm the gap-opening PDW structure.
why_interesting: The mechanism provides a general framework for understanding symmetry breaking in superconductors that does not require exotic topological features, making it relevant to many unconventional pairing theories.
